The story is tightly constructed and follows a clear, logical progression as Marlen enters and moves through her childhood home. Every sensory detail and observation—the muscle memory of turning the key, the coat on the hook, her reflection in the mirror, and the faded note in the kitchen—contributes to the overarching themes of memory, grief, and the passage of time. Notably, the "impossible" scent of lavender introduced in the beginning is woven back into the ending, successfully binding the narrative elements together to build an eerie, lingering mystery that makes the story feel complete and unified.
